properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 29 at 6:30PM MDT until October 29 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 630 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Portions of Jornada Experimental Range.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 845 PM MDT THIS EVENING FOR NORTH CENTRAL DONA ANA COUNTY

properties.areaDesc: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 2:07PM HST until October 29 at 5:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Windward Big Island

* WHEN...Until 500 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 204 PM HST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain over Windward
Big Island. Rain was falling at a rate of 1 to 2 inches per hour
with the heaviest rain over the Hilo and Puna districts. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hilo, Hawaiian Paradise Park, Kapaau, Honokaa, Honomu, Papaikou,
Pepeekeo, Hakalau, Ninole, Laupahoehoe, Mountain View and
Glenwood.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from streams, drainage ditches and low lying areas prone to
flooding.

A Flood Watch is also in effect for the Big Island until 6 PM HST.

This advisory replaces the previous advisory that was in effect for
the island of Hawaii in Hawaii County.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 5 PM HST THIS AFTERNOON FOR THE ISLAND OF HAWAII IN HAWAII COUNTY

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 845 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 537 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Up to 0.75 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall of up to 0.5 inches is expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Las Cruces, NMSU Main Campus, Talavera and San Pablo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 3:38PM AKDT until October 30 at 4:15PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.


* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 415 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Light rainfall will gradually increase in intensity this evening
and continue through Friday morning before the rain slowly tapers
off Friday afternoon. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an
inch per hour are possible between 10 PM tonight and 10 AM
Friday, with a storm total between 3 and 4 inches of rain likely
with this event. Prolonged heavy rain may lead to areas of
flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor
drainage areas, and ponding of water on roadways.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 2:39PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
ESFABQ

* IMPACTS...River, creek, washes and arroyos may reach out of
banks. Rock, mud and debris may flow into roadways and flash
flooding can not be ruled out, especially in urban areas.

* CONFIDENCE...High confidence in widespread rainfall, with low
confidence in river and flash flooding.

* WHAT...A strong Pacific storm system will interact with a
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest and Four
Corners region, producing widespread rain which will focus in
the mountains.

* WHERE...Four Corners and surrounding region, including Aztec,
Bloomfield, Farmington and Shiprock.

* WHEN...Sunday into Monday.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...River basins are already saturated from
last week's rainfall and flooding, making additional runoff more
efficient and can more easily cause flooding problems. The
greatest precipitation amounts are forecast in the San Juan
Mountains of Colorado, which will create high flows in the
Animas and La Plata Rivers. These rivers feed the San Juan
River, which saw record flooding last week.

Continue to monitor forecasts for the updates as this situation
unfolds.

Follow NWS Albuquerque on Facebook at: www.facebook.com/NWSAlbuquerque
and on X at: www.x.com/NWSAlbuquerque

management officials.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Oregon and southwest

* WHEN...From midnight Friday Night to 9 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Frost and freeze headlines are only issued
through the growing season of April 1 through October 31.
Therefore, frost or freeze headlines will not be issued beginning
November 1, even though similar low temperatures are possible.
Additionally, frost and freeze headlines will no longer be issued
this growing season for the Upper Hood River Valley, southern
Willamette Valley, south Washington Cascade Foothills, and north
Oregon Coast Range as these locations have already experienced a
hard freeze earlier in October.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 1:56PM EDT until October 30 at 3:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Nassau County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM EDT Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Friday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Sullivan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 29 at 1:53PM EDT by NWS Binghamton NY
properties.description:
The combination of dry fuels, gusty northwest winds to 30 mph,
and minimum relative humidity values of 40 to 45 percent will
contribute to an elevated risk of fire spread for Sullivan County.
The lowest relative humidity and strongest wind gusts are expected
during the late morning to mid afternoon hours on Friday.

Use extra caution if handling any potential ignition sources such
as machinery or matches, and ensure to properly extinguish or
dispose of cigarette butts.

NWSheadline: Elevated Risk Of Fire Spread Late Friday Morning Through Friday Afternoon

properties.areaDesc: South Central Mountains
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 11:52AM MDT until October 29 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorms are expected to develop near the ridgeline of the
Sacramento Mountains this afternoon.  Storm motions of
south-to-north at 10-15 mph could also lead to several rounds of
storms passing over or near the burn scar areas.  There is
potential for 1 to 1.5 inches of rain to fall where two or more
storms impact the same area.

Additional rainfall is expected overnight, but rainfall rates
will be lower.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 29 at 1:51PM EDT until October 30 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through late Sunday night. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO; Dolores, CO; La Plata, CO; Montezuma, CO; San Miguel, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

Low pressure begins to dig southward from the PACNW on Friday,
tapping into a fetch of Pacific moisture that will evolve into an
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest this weekend.
Showers and thunderstorms develop on Friday and Saturday across the
region. Lighter rainfall totals Friday and Saturday will reflect,
initially lower, moisture. However, a few thunderstorms could produce
impactful downpours on saturated soils left over from last weekend's
historic rainfall.

Deeper moisture develops Saturday night and early Sunday. This is
expected to produce heavier and more widespread rainfall across
southeast UT and southwest CO Sunday and Monday, mostly below 10000
feet. While rivers are forecast to remain below action stage, a
growing concern lies in the potential for runoff around saturated
hillsides in the region. This could produce rock, mud, and debris
flows onto roadways, as well as flash flood prone burn scars, washes,
slot canyons, and arroyos. Early estimates predict an area of 1 to 2
inches of new rainfall for portions of southeast UT and southwest CO.

This is a preliminary forecast that hinges on slight shifts in a
strong moisture plume impacting the region. It also attempts to
capture the most statistically likely outcome, despite stronger and
weaker outlier predictions. Outdoor enthusiasts, motorists, and
residents of recent flood impacted areas are encouraged to remain
abreast of the developing forecast in the coming days.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 3:45AM HST until October 29 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough over the eastern half of the state will continue to focus
return showers to the islands through the day. Pockets of heavy rain
and isolated thunderstorms may produce flash flooding over Maui and
Hawaii Counties.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Molokai, Lanai, Maui, Kahoolawe and Big Island.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A trough continues to lay over the eastern half of the state
within a very moist and fairly unstable environment. Energy
moving up from the southwest may initiate return periods of
moderate to locally heavy rainfall. This rain has a high
probability of focusing on Maui and Hawaii Counties. Locally
moderate to heavy showers, with possible isolated thunderstorms,
may produce short-lived intense rain rates through the day.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 29 at 9:16AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River are slowing flow at Astor, which is also impacting river
levels upstream.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Thursday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...At Astor, river levels are forecast to slowly decline
but remain in Moderate Flood Stage for at least the next couple
weeks. Additional rises are possible as onshore winds
periodically increase.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...South Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 638 PM MDT, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Flooding was reported in Socorro County in the Escondida and
Pueblito Communities. Several roads have been rendered impassible
near San Pedro.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Socorro, San Antonio, Bosque Del Apache Refuge, Escondida,
Lemitar, San Acacia, Laborcita, Luis Lopez and Chamizal.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 28 at 3:46PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend and early this week. Around 0.25
to 0.50" of additional rain is expected by the end of the week which
will keep water levels high. No flooding is expected but those along
the rivers and streams should be vigilant of the high water that is
expected through the end of the week.
